subject: Banking
title: How Mortgages Generate Billions
description: A micro-lesson that makes How Mortgages Generate Billions usable.

hook.text: US banks hold $12 trillion in mortgage debt. A 30-year mortgage at 7% pays the bank more in interest than the home.

buildup.text: A $400,000 mortgage at 7% over 30 years costs $558,000 in interest alone. The borrower pays nearly $1 million total.

discovery.text: Banks also charge origination fees of 0.5-1%. On a $400,000 loan, that's $2,000-$4,000 before a single payment is made.

twist.text: Banks often sell mortgages to investors and keep the servicing fee. They profit without holding the risk.

climax.text: Mortgages are the ultimate banking product. Long duration, secured by real property, and profitable at every stage.

punchline.text: $558,000 in interest on a $400,000 loan. Mortgages are profit machines.

quiz.question: How much interest does a $400,000 mortgage at 7% generate over 30 years?

details.summary: Mortgages are the largest asset class on most bank balance sheets, generating revenue through origination fees, interest income, servicing fees, and securitization profits. The US mortgage market exceeds $12 trillion in outstanding balances.
details.whyItMatters: Mortgages connect banks to the housing market, the largest store of household wealth. How banks profit from mortgages affects home prices, housing affordability, and the financial stability of millions of families.
takeaways: US bank mortgage holdings exceed $12 trillion in outstanding balances
Banks earn from origination fees, interest spreads, and servicing contracts
Securitization allows banks to sell mortgages and earn fees while removing risk

faq.question: How many ways do banks profit from a single mortgage?
faq.answer: Banks earn an origination fee at closing, collect interest over the loan's life, charge servicing fees for managing payments, and can sell the mortgage as a security for an additional gain. Some earn from mortgage insurance requirements as well.

faq.question: Why do banks sell mortgages instead of keeping them?
faq.answer: Selling mortgages frees up capital to make new loans and removes interest rate risk from the balance sheet. The bank still earns origination and servicing fees while passing the long-term credit and rate risk to investors.
